descriptionChirho: Masculine noun תָּא (ta'): a chamber or guard room, specifically the side rooms flanking the gates of Ezekiel's visionary temple (Ezek 40:7-36) and the guard chambers in the temple/palace of Solomon (1 Kgs 14:28; 2 Chr 12:11). In Ezekiel's temple vision, the תָּאִים are the small chambers (typically three on each side) built into the thickness of the gateway walls, serving as guard posts. The noun appears with ketiv/qere variants (כתיב תאו / קרי תָּאָיו 'its chambers') throughout Ezekiel 40. Arabic حُجْرَة/حُجُرَات 'room/chambers,' Korean 방/방들 'room/rooms,' German Kammer 'chamber,' Spanish camara 'chamber,' Hindi कोठरी/कोठरियाँ 'small room/rooms,' French chambre. Possibly an Aramaism (cf. Aramaic תָּא, Arabic ثَوَى 'to dwell'). All five auto-clusters represent the same architectural term, split by singular/plural, construct/absolute, and ketiv/qere variants.
